User_Story: As a capstone team member, I want a GitHub repository with README and wiki, so that project work is organized and trackable.
Business_Value: Establishes the shared project foundation and documentation entry point.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Repository foundation setup | Given a new project repository | When the team initializes the repo and wiki | Then the repository contains the core project metadata | And team members can access the documentation location.
Test_Case: Open the repository and wiki links and verify the project README and team information are present.

User_Story: As a developer, I want a runnable Python and Next.js project skeleton, so that implementation can start from a working baseline.
Business_Value: Reduces startup friction for Sprint 1 development.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Initial application skeleton | Given the repository is cloned | When dependencies are installed for Python and platform services | Then both application layers bootstrap successfully | And development can proceed on a working structure.
Test_Case: Run editable Python install and platform dependency install and verify no fatal bootstrap errors.

User_Story: As an evaluator, I want YAML-based scenarios and a loader baseline, so that evaluation cases are configurable and reusable.
Business_Value: Creates a scalable way to define and manage evaluation scenarios.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Scenario definition loading | Given valid and invalid scenario YAML files | When the loader processes them | Then valid scenarios load successfully | And invalid scenarios fail with clear validation errors.
Test_Case: Run scenario loader checks against valid and invalid YAML examples.

User_Story: As a scrum team, I want standard templates for stories, acceptance criteria, and sprint artifacts, so that grading deliverables stay consistent.
Business_Value: Improves quality and consistency of sprint documentation.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Sprint documentation template setup | Given the team is preparing sprint artifacts | When templates are defined for stories and evidence | Then required fields are standardized | And future sprint documentation follows the same structure.
Test_Case: Review the template columns and sample sprint artifact structure for consistency.

User_Story: As a RAG Engineer, I want a health endpoint on the target agent, so that platform connectivity checks are deterministic.
Business_Value: Supports reliable readiness checks before evaluation.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Target agent health validation | Given the target agent is running | When the platform or user calls the health endpoint | Then the service returns a healthy response | And connectivity can be confirmed before evaluation.
Test_Case: Call GET /health on the built-in agent and verify HTTP 200 plus service status data.

User_Story: As a RAG Engineer, I want a stable /agent contract, so that the evaluator can call my service consistently.
Business_Value: Improves interoperability between the target agent and the evaluation framework.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Target agent query contract | Given a valid query payload | When the client calls POST /agent | Then the service returns an answer payload | And the response includes the expected fields for downstream evaluation.
Test_Case: Send a POST /agent request and validate answer

User_Story: As an AI Application Developer, I want to register and ping my agent endpoint, so that I can validate connectivity before running evaluations.
Business_Value: Reduces failed runs caused by invalid or unavailable endpoints.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Agent connectivity check | Given a valid agent base URL | When the user runs a connection test | Then the platform confirms the agent is reachable | And actionable feedback is shown for success or failure.
Test_Case: Use /api/agent/ping with valid and invalid URLs and verify platform responses.

User_Story: As an AI Application Developer, I want a playground to send prompts to my agent, so that I can inspect raw behavior before red-team evaluation.
Business_Value: Improves debugging and demo clarity before full scenario execution.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Pre-evaluation sandbox query | Given a connected agent and a user prompt | When the user sends a query from the sandbox | Then the platform shows the agent response | And any available metadata or context is displayed.
Test_Case: Use /sandbox and POST /api/agent/query to verify response rendering.

User_Story: As an AI Safety Engineer, I want to run a scenario bundle against an agent, so that I can detect safety and reliability violations.
Business_Value: Creates a repeatable workflow for agent safety validation.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Scenario bundle execution | Given configured provider settings and selected scenarios | When an evaluation starts | Then the run moves through execution states correctly | And scenario-level results are stored for review.
Test_Case: Create a run from /dashboard/evaluations/new and verify status transitions plus persisted results.

User_Story: As an AI Safety Engineer, I want predicate-based scoring, so that unsafe outputs are flagged with severity.
Business_Value: Standardizes risk assessment across evaluation runs.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Severity-based scoring | Given evaluation outputs containing safe and unsafe behaviors | When the scoring engine grades them | Then harmful outputs receive failure labels | And safe refusals or expected behaviors receive passing results.
Test_Case: Run scoring tests and validate PASS

User_Story: As an AI Safety Engineer, I want JSON, Markdown, and HTML reports, so that I can provide reviewable evaluation evidence.
Business_Value: Enables both machine-readable and human-readable reporting artifacts.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Evaluation artifact generation | Given a completed evaluation | When report generation runs | Then JSON, Markdown, and HTML artifacts are produced | And each reflects the stored evaluation results.
Test_Case: Download generated reports and verify they are non-empty and structurally valid.

User_Story: As an Evaluation Operator, I want evaluation pages to auto-refresh while runs are active, so that I do not need manual navigation.
Business_Value: Improves visibility and usability during live demos and monitoring.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Live result page refresh | Given an evaluation is queued or running | When the detail page is open | Then the page refreshes status automatically | And refresh stops after the run reaches a terminal state.
Test_Case: Keep an evaluation page open during execution and verify automatic updates through completion.

User_Story: As an AI Application Developer, I want summary metrics to match detailed report data, so that score interpretation is trustworthy.
Business_Value: Prevents inconsistencies between UI summaries and report artifacts.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Report summary normalization | Given a completed evaluation with stored result data | When the platform computes summary metrics | Then the summary matches the detailed report contents | And the displayed counts and scores remain consistent.
Test_Case: Compare UI summary values with the downloaded JSON report for the same evaluation.

User_Story: As a DevOps Engineer, I want CI to execute evaluations automatically, so that unsafe regressions are caught before merge.
Business_Value: Adds automated quality gates to the engineering workflow.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: CI evaluation execution | Given a code change triggers the workflow | When the GitHub Actions evaluation job runs | Then the workflow executes the evaluation steps | And generated reports are uploaded as artifacts when available.
Test_Case: Trigger the workflow and verify evaluation execution plus artifact upload behavior.

User_Story: As an AI Safety Engineer, I want broader scenario coverage across jailbreak, prompt injection, PII, hallucination, and related risks, so that evaluation reflects real-world attack patterns.
Business_Value: Improves the depth and realism of red-team testing.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Expanded scenario catalog loading | Given the scenario directory contains the full library | When scenarios are loaded and executed | Then the platform recognizes the expanded scenario set | And evaluations can run across multiple threat categories.
Test_Case: Load the scenario catalog and verify broad coverage categories are available for selection and execution.

Persona: Enterprise AI Safety and Compliance Engineer
User_Story: As an Enterprise AI Safety and Compliance Engineer, I want release-gate decisions with policy-based GO or BLOCK results, so that I can determine whether an agent is safe for deployment.
Business_Value: Supports formal release governance using evaluation evidence.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Release-gate policy enforcement | Given a completed release-candidate evaluation | When the policy gate is checked | Then the system returns a GO or BLOCK decision | And the decision is based on configured policy rules.
Test_Case: Use the release gate flow and verify policy-driven decision output for a completed evaluation.

Persona: Enterprise AI Safety and Compliance Engineer
User_Story: As an Enterprise AI Safety and Compliance Engineer, I want downloadable evidence artifacts, so that audit packages can be reviewed externally.
Business_Value: Improves traceability and supports compliance review workflows.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Evidence artifact generation | Given a completed evaluation | When the user requests an evidence artifact | Then the platform returns the artifact successfully | And the artifact corresponds to the evaluation result set.
Test_Case: Download the evidence artifact from the evaluation detail page or API and verify file generation.

User_Story: As a RAG Engineer, I want grounding, contradiction, and missing-context scenarios, so that hallucinations and unsupported answers are measurable.
Business_Value: Improves reliability testing for retrieval-grounded agents.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: RAG reliability scenario execution | Given a RAG-targeted evaluation run | When grounding and contradiction scenarios are executed | Then unsupported or incorrect behaviors are surfaced | And grounded responses are evaluated against expectations.
Test_Case: Run RAG-specific scenarios and inspect failure reasons related to missing context or contradiction.

User_Story: As an Evaluation Operator, I want clearer monitoring for evaluation progress, so that long-running jobs are easier to manage.
Business_Value: Improves operational visibility for evaluation execution.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Evaluation progress visibility | Given an evaluation is active | When the user opens monitoring views | Then the platform shows current run status clearly | And the user can distinguish active, completed, and failed states.
Test_Case: Use evaluation detail and list views to verify status visibility across active and terminal runs.

User_Story: As a Platform Team Member, I want batch evaluation for multiple agent candidates, so that I can compare variants using the same scenario set.
Business_Value: Enables side-by-side comparison of competing agent versions before release.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Batch candidate evaluation | Given multiple configured agent candidates and a shared scenario bundle | When the user starts a batch run | Then the platform creates evaluations for each candidate | And aggregated comparison results are produced.
Test_Case: Create a batch from /dashboard/batches/new and verify batch execution plus comparison output.

User_Story: As a Platform Team Member, I want regression comparison across runs, so that I can detect quality drops before release.
Business_Value: Helps prevent shipping weaker agent behavior than the baseline.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Baseline regression analysis | Given a baseline result and a candidate result | When the platform compares them | Then regressions are identified | And the comparison is surfaced in the results workflow.
Test_Case: Use the regression flow and verify baseline-versus-candidate comparison results.

User_Story: As a Compliance Engineer, I want threat-model coverage checks, so that I can verify required safety categories before approval.
Business_Value: Ensures release evaluations cover enterprise threat areas instead of isolated scenarios.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Threat coverage validation | Given a set of selected release scenarios | When the platform checks threat coverage | Then covered and missing categories are identified | And release readiness is blocked when required coverage is incomplete.
Test_Case: Use the coverage flow and verify missing versus covered threat categories for a release setup.

User_Story: As an Admin or Release Manager, I want versioned release-gate policies, so that I can activate and manage policy changes over time.
Business_Value: Supports controlled policy evolution across evaluation cycles.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Policy version activation | Given multiple release-gate policy versions | When an administrator activates one version | Then the chosen policy becomes active | And subsequent gate checks use that version.
Test_Case: Use the policy management flow or API to create and activate a release-gate policy version.

User_Story: As an Enterprise Admin, I want role-based controls for evaluator, release manager, and admin workflows, so that sensitive actions are restricted appropriately.
Business_Value: Protects governance and operational actions from unauthorized use.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Role-based access enforcement | Given a user with a defined application role | When the user attempts a restricted action | Then access is allowed or denied based on role | And the platform enforces the permission boundary consistently.
Test_Case: Verify restricted workflows behave differently for allowed versus disallowed roles.

User_Story: As an AI Platform Owner, I want drift monitoring across historical and current runs, so that I can detect quality changes over time.
Business_Value: Adds post-release oversight for long-term model or agent behavior changes.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Drift analysis execution | Given baseline historical results and current evaluation data | When a drift check runs | Then the platform reports quality changes over time | And the results are available for review.
Test_Case: Use the drift monitoring flow and verify baseline-versus-current analysis output.

User_Story: As an AI Platform Owner, I want signed audit alerts for important evaluation events, so that external systems can trust notifications.
Business_Value: Supports enterprise monitoring and downstream audit pipelines.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Signed audit event emission | Given a configured webhook and a relevant evaluation event | When the platform emits an audit event | Then the payload is signed | And the receiving system can validate the event source.
Test_Case: Trigger an audit test event and verify signed webhook behavior through the audit event flow.

User_Story: As an AI Safety Engineer, I want targeted adversarial scenario generation by threat type, so that I can expand red-team coverage quickly.
Business_Value: Speeds creation of new scenarios aligned with threat categories.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Adversarial scenario generation | Given a selected threat category and a generation request | When the user generates scenarios | Then the platform returns targeted scenario content | And the generated scenarios can be reviewed or persisted.
Test_Case: Use /api/scenarios/generate-adversarial and verify output for a chosen threat category.

User_Story: As an External Client or CI User, I want scoped API keys, so that I can trigger evaluations without relying on browser sessions.
Business_Value: Enables automation and external integration with the platform.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: API key-based access | Given a valid tenant API key | When the client calls a supported evaluation endpoint | Then the platform authenticates the request | And the operation succeeds according to the granted scope.
Test_Case: Use a tenant API key against supported evaluation endpoints and verify authenticated access.

User_Story: As an External Evaluator, I want a bring-your-agent onboarding flow, so that I can connect my own HTTP agent without cloning the repository.
Business_Value: Broadens platform usability for external evaluators and demos.
Acceptance_Criteria: Scenario: Self-serve external agent onboarding | Given an external HTTP agent URL | When the user connects, detects, tests, and runs a quick evaluation | Then the platform completes onboarding through the browser | And the agent can be evaluated without local code changes.
Test_Case: Use /bring-your-agent and verify connect
